findings.sentence: 45 of the 164 mineral baby and kids sunscreen formulas listed in the FDA's DailyMed label database contain butyloctyl salicylate. It is not an FDA sunscreen active ingredient; its manufacturer says it can contribute to SPF (no more than 2 SPF units at 5%) and help prevent some UV filters from breaking down.
findings.population: unique formulations of sunscreen labels that say baby or kids (FDA DailyMed; selected by rule from the label, with edge cases decided by hand and every decision recorded with its reason); mineral-only actives (zinc oxide and/or titanium dioxide)
findings.caveat: DailyMed lists drug labels submitted to the FDA, including labels for products made in US facilities for other markets. A listing is not proof that a product is on US shelves today.

source.title: FDA DailyMed SPL registry (structured product labels), ARW House analysis

findings.legal_framing: Not a violation: butyloctyl salicylate is not an FDA sunscreen active, so it belongs with the inactive ingredients, as the rules require. The finding is about how labels work, not about any brand.
